page.title: What is included in Community as a Service?
page.description: Learn the full checklist of strategy, platform choice, moderation, programming and reporting that a Community as a Service engagement delivers, with platform comparison table and practical next steps.
page.h1: What is included in Community as a Service?
page.definition: Community as a Service is a managed offering that provides strategy, platform selection, moderation, programming, onboarding and reporting for online communities, delivered by a dedicated team that owns each workstream and measures health monthly and aligns activities with business goals.
page.quick_answer: Start by defining purpose, audience segments and success metrics, then choose a platform that matches your moderation needs and programming cadence.

sections.h2: What strategy and planning does Community as a Service cover?

blocks.p: It starts with a community strategy that defines purpose, audience segments, value propositions and success metrics.

ul: Value proposition design for each segment
Success metric selection and baseline measurement

sections.h2: Which platforms are commonly used and how do they compare?

blocks.p: The service evaluates the major community platforms and matches them to your use case.

sections.h2: What moderation and member support tasks are included?

blocks.p: Moderation covers policy enforcement, escalation paths, real‑time chat oversight and member‑level support.

ul: Escalation matrix with response time targets
Real‑time monitoring of chat and forums
Member onboarding assistance and welcome sequences

sections.h2: How is programming and onboarding structured?

blocks.p: Programming delivers recurring events, content series and onboarding journeys that move members from newcomer to advocate.

ol: Design annual content calendar with themes
Produce event run‑of‑show and speaker briefs
Run live sessions with producer and backup stream
Capture recordings and create highlight clips
Distribute follow‑up resources and next‑step calls to action
Iterate programming based on engagement feedback

sections.h2: What reporting and ongoing optimisation are delivered?

blocks.p: Reporting provides monthly health dashboards, engagement trends and actionable recommendations for the next cycle.

ul: Activity heatmap by channel and time zone
Sentiment snapshot from surveys and keywords
Content performance by format and topic
Churn risk flags for at‑risk segments
Prioritised optimisation backlog for next quarter

faq.q: How long does a typical Community as a Service engagement last?
faq.a: A first plan runs ninety days, long enough to see a trend and short enough to change course; longer engagements extend month by month based on scope and evolving goals.

faq.q: What is the pricing model for Community as a Service?
faq.a: West Peek Productions quotes by scope covering coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming; there is no fixed price list, so you send the scope for a custom quote.

faq.q: Which platforms does the service support?
faq.a: Common platforms include Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic and LinkedIn groups; the team can also work on a custom or self‑hosted solution if required.

faq.q: Can the service handle hybrid community events?
faq.a: Yes, the team produces virtual and hybrid events on the platform you already use, providing run‑of‑show, speaker rehearsal, live producer, backup stream and edited recordings.
